text: [{"rune": "Ansuz", "text": "Behind the last rise there was more slope than you could see from below, and now that it is behind you the breath comes slow and full. Ansuz is that breath returning, the air moving free where the climb had held it tight. The grain waits to be cut, and you are standing where the ground finally levels."}]

[{"rune": "Ansuz", "text": "Behind you the slope you climbed is out of sight now, and the air up here is thinner than the air you started in. Ansuz is the breath finding its own pace again before you move. Stand a moment and let it settle."}]

[{"rune":"Ansuz","text":"Behind the crest, the grain fields remain out of sight as you finish the slope and your breath returns more slowly than expected. Ansuz gives direction room to be heard between breaths. The wider path stays quiet until your pace and breathing meet."}]

[{"rune":"Ansuz","text":"What is out of sight is the ridge you just climbed, the slope falling away behind while your breath takes its time to meet you. In this grain-cutting month the air clears your head, and Ansuz works as exchange between breath and direction. You stand still long enough to hear the higher pattern in the wind, then you move with that plain note held steady."}]

There is a rawness in this â new growth bruises easily, and what stands between you has not yet grown roots deep enough to hold in wind."}, {"rune": "Sowilo", "text": "If you keep walking as you walk now, the sun breaks through and glints on the wet stones, and each one shows its true colour in the light. Where the ice once held everything still, the thaw runs clear and the stones between you stand plain to see."}]

[{"rune": "Isa", "text": "Rain lay over these stones a long while, and nothing on them moved or dried. Water held in every hollow, and the cold in it was not something you could hurry."}, {"rune": "Berkana", "text": "Now the light comes through and the wet rock glints, and in the cracks where the damp sat longest, green is standing up. What grows there does so because the stone stayed wet, not in spite of it â though the same water that feeds it can also make the footing slick, and two people crossing this ground will not always find the same stone steady."}, {"rune": "Sowilo", "text": "Keep walking as you walk now, and the sun climbs high enough to dry the ledges, and you see the whole slope plain â where the moss holds, where the rock is bare, where the other one stands. [{"rune":"Isa","text":"What was held in stillness has already taken its shape, and the wet stones remember where the ice lay between two people."},{"rune":"Berkana","text":"Now, with two months of summer left, small growth reaches into that cleared space. It needs care from both sides, yet care alone cannot settle what remains unspoken."},{"rune":"Sowilo","text":"If the present course continues, the sun breaks through and shows the ground more plainly, including the parts that do not meet. What was fixed under ice now stands visible in sunlight, glinting on the wet stones where two paths touch."}]

[{"rune":"Isa","text":"The sun finally breaks through and glints on the wet stones, but before this there is only the slick chill of pause, breath held, feet careful on the ford where two paths meet and neither moves."},{"rune":"Berkana","text":"Now the light stays a little longer on those stones, the water warms, a tender green pushes from the bank, you speak or fall quiet more gently, you make room for small shoots without forcing them tall."},{"rune":"Sowilo","text":"Keep walking like this and the wet stones show their shapes plain in the noon light, what is firm and what is loose stands out, and crossing stops being guesswork as the sun lays a clear path over the riverâs skin."}]
